section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Plane and the Cone
section_1.content: Briefly introduce the 'Double Cone' (a cone extending infinitely in both directions) and a cutting plane. Define the intersection as a conic section. Establish the visual goal: understanding why a slice of a cone results in circles, ellipses, parabolas, or hyperbolas.
section_1.example: Imagine a magician slicing a carrot cone with a knife; the angle of the blade determines the shape of the cut.

section_2.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Introduce the Dandelin Spheres—two spheres placed inside the cone such that they are tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point). These points of tangency are the 'Foci' of our conic section.
section_2.example: Visualize two glowing bubbles trapped inside a cone, pressed against a flat glass plate, touching it at two specific glowing dots.

section_3.title: The Geometry of the Ellipse
section_3.content: Demonstrate the Ellipse. Show the plane intersecting only the top half of the cone. Explain that for any point P on the ellipse, the sum of the distances to the two tangency points (foci) is constant—the key definition of an ellipse.
section_3.example: A hiker (the point P) trekking on a tilted landscape where the sum of distances to two marked basecamps remains constant.

section_4.title: Transitions: Parabolas and Hyperbolas
section_4.content: Explain how changing the plane's angle changes the number of spheres trapped. When the plane is parallel to the cone's side (one sphere), it forms a Parabola. When the plane slices both halves (two spheres), it forms a Hyperbola.
section_4.example: A satellite dish (Parabola) capturing signals versus a dual-lens telescope (Hyperbola) focusing light from two distinct directions.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap the beauty of the Dandelin construction: it bridges the gap between 3D solids and 2D geometry. Highlight that the 'magic points' of tangency are the foundation for orbit mechanics in physics.
section_5.example: The orbits of planets around the Sun (a focus of the ellipse) are the real-world manifestation of the Dandelin principle in action.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right side of screen (from x=2 to x=6)
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.7
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.7
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
